subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm working out realistic proportions for the scene—a small red-eyed tree frog around 5-6cm resting on a larger leaf roughly 20-22cm long, keeping the leaf mostly flat with a slight stem detail.

I'm figuring out how the leaf and stem need to touch the ground plane at y=0, extruding the leaf shape flat with a thin stem bending down to the floor, while positioning the frog's crouched body resting just above the leaf surface with legs folded, and starting to lay out the skeleton joints for the spine and hips.

I'm now sketching the spine chain from hips to head with coordinates along the z-axis, then sweeping the body geometry along that chain with a radius function to shape the torso, and applying a green-to-cream countershading paint scheme with a flank stripe based on surface normals.

For the head, I'm considering whether to extend the body sweep forward into a blunt snout or model it as a separate scaled sphere attached at the head joint, with the jaw as a small flattened piece on its own joint.

Still working out eye geometry...

Adjusting iris radius to 0.0065 at offset 0.0112 keeps the edges within the eye surface, which checks out. For the pupil slit, I'm working out how the aimed sphere's local axes orient so I can scale it thin and vertical to form a proper slit shape.

Now I'm thinking about eye color (a deep red), deciding to skip any eyelid or brow detail since it's not necessary, and moving on to small dark spheres for the nostrils while skipping an explicit mouth line.

Working out the folded hind leg geometry now—placing hip, knee, ankle, and foot points to create a frog-like crouched pose with the foot resting flat on the leaf surface, checking the vertical positions so the toes sit just above the leaf's top edge.

Toes extend forward from the ankle, so I'll build the hind leg as a four-point chain (hip, knee, ankle, foot) with tapering radius from thigh to toe, and paint it using the same flank countershading as the body for continuity.

Placing toe chains with single spans per digit, orange coloring with slightly lighter orange pad discs flattened at the tips, sized smaller for front toes than hind, positioned at leaf height with pad centers slightly raised.

Deciding to skip explicit webbing and tarsus coloring, instead using a color band transition along the leg sweep so the lower portion near the toes shifts to orange automatically. Now starting to lay out front leg joint positions, beginning with shoulder and elbow coordinates.

Defining a function to build mirrored limbs, then setting up the spine chain with four points and three segments named spine1-3, attaching the head joint to the last spine segment.

Now I'm working out hip and arm attachment points along the spine, and designing a radius function that tapers the body's width and height along its length to give a widest point near the hips using a sine-based profile.

Working out the belly and flank coloring based on normal direction: cream underside, blue flanks with alternating vertical bars bordered by cream stripes near the top, mimicking real frog markings.

I'm bumping the paint texture size up to 2048 to keep resolution reasonable across the body, leaf, and other elements, and adding subtle green mottling noise to the body region to avoid flat color.

For the head, I'm placing it at the head joint with its own scale, overlapping the body front slightly. I want a similar top-green/bottom-cream paint pattern but restricted so the flank bars don't bleed onto the head, giving the head simpler plain shading instead.

For the lower jaw, I'm adding a smaller sphere positioned slightly below and forward of the head center, using a similar green-to-cream countershade. I'm defining its joint ("jaw") as a child of the head, hinged near the rear so it can open downward.

I need to double-check the overlap math so the jaw doesn't protrude past the head's taper at that height — adjusting the jaw's scale and z-offset slightly to avoid sticking out beyond the head silhouette.

Jaw fits within head bounds now. Settling on head scale and position, placing large eyes at the sides with slight inset so they sit naturally against the head surface, then starting to work out pupil direction for the left eye.

Now computing nostril placement — small dark spheres positioned just below the eyes using the head's ellipsoid surface equation to find the right z-depth, keeping them tiny. Skipping eyelids, brows, and throat details for simplicity, and moving on to laying out the leaf shape as a pointed outline in the xz-plane spanning roughly 0.24 in length.

Making the tip and base vertices sharp, extruding the leaf shape with thin depth, and positioning it with the right orientation vectors. Adding a darker green color and planning thin midrib and vein rods in a lighter green to overlay on top of the leaf surface for texture.

Now I'm plotting side vein pairs branching from the midrib at varying widths down the leaf length to mimic natural narrowing, then starting to sweep the stem curve downward from the leaf base toward the floor.

The stem path curves through a few control points down to near ground level with a thin tapering radius, touching y=0. I'm considering adding a small soil disc at the base so the stem has something to visually root into rather than floating at the floor plane.

Adding the base disc and rigging the stem to a root joint, with a simple bone chain so the spine and leaf parts all parent off that root. Still thinking through colors—brown soil, cream frog belly.

Now I'm working out the hind foot toes, setting each toe's base position and spreading them at small yaw angles from forward with slightly varying lengths, then building a one-segment chain per toe parented to the foot joint for rigging.

I'm adding toe pads: small flattened spheres sitting at each toe tip, colored amber, bone-attached to the first joint of the toe chain, with the toe sweep tapering slightly toward the tip. Now I'm starting on the hand, beginning with the wrist position.

Now I'm working through the hind leg proportions — hip, knee, and ankle positions and radii — making sure the shin segment connects the knee to the ankle with consistent joint placement relative to the body width.

Continuing the elbow and wrist placement, then setting up toe directions with yaw angles for splayed digits. I'm working out the mirroring logic so left and right limbs share one function with x-sign flipped, plus a naming convention for joints like hipHR, and noting the frog's hands should reach forward under the head toward the ground.

Now I'm defining the body paint function: a lime-green base blended with a darker lime via noise-based mottling, switching to cream on the underside (belly), with core colors set as lime, lime2, cream, and blue for later use.

I'll slant the bar pattern by factoring in n.y for a diagonal stripe effect, keep body sides at 10 for smoother shading, and skip extras like throat pouch, eyelids, and dorsal spots to keep things simple while still achieving that wide-eyed surprised look through the pupils alone.

For the body sweep, I need to fix the radius function's return type—TypeScript wants a tuple `[number, number]` rather than a generic array, so I'll annotate it explicitly. For the head, I'm using a scaled sphere geometry and making sure the paint function correctly composes the scale transform with the world matrix so normals stay correct in model space.

Now I'm painting the head and jaw with color functions based on normal direction (cream underside, green elsewhere), giving the eyes a solid red color, and setting up the joint hierarchy—attaching head and jaw joints to the spine chain with specific positions and directions.

For the spine and legs, I'm building chains from arrays of points, using catmull smoothing so the skin rounds the corners nicely instead of having sharp polyline joints.

I'm setting the leg's parent joint to attach to the appropriate spine joint (hind legs to joint 0, arms to joint 2), then sweeping the tube along each chain with a radius array and color bands, working out the arc-length positions for where the band cuts should land given the short hock-to-ankle segment lengths.

Now I'm sizing the arm chain similarly, placing the hand band around 0.9 with its own tapering radii, and setting up a toe-generation function that takes a parent joint, base position, side, splay angles, and length to build each toe with consistent tip height.

Choosing orange tones for the toes and pads to give the feet a warm, grounded color accent.

Adding small liveliness details to the eyes: a tiny cream highlight sphere offset toward the front-top of each eye to simulate a light reflection, while skipping the extra eyelid ridge to keep things simple. Now I'm moving into writing the actual eye construction code, looping over left and right sides to set up their centers and features.

Still writing eye geometry...

Adding sphere helper and leaf extrusion code...

Still defining stem and soil geometry...

Now I need unique joint naming for toes and limbs, like "toeHL1" for hind-left and "toeFL1" for fore-left, plus a limb-building function that sets up hind-leg polyline chains parented to the spine with hip joint names.

Still writing toe geometry...

I'm adjusting toe pad placement, tweaking the y-position so the pad sinks slightly into the leaf surface rather than floating, balancing toe height against the sweep radius and ankle joint position.

That gap looks fine for the ankle joint. Nearest hand positioning is settled, dorsal coloring just needs a touch of cream or dark accent, and now I'm setting up the builder call with a 2048 paint size for the red-eyed tree frog model.
